shorts.title: What you will learn: Encapsulation
shorts.hook: A class can protect its own rules.
shorts.script: A class can protect its own rules. Today we see why classes hide their data. The class checks every change, so it never ends up in a bad state. Encapsulation means hiding the data and offering checked functions. A setter can refuse a bad value. A getter lets others read the value. Then the class always stays valid. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Encapsulation.

shorts.title: Encapsulation in one minute
shorts.hook: Encapsulation means hiding the data and offering checked functions.
shorts.script: Encapsulation means hiding the data and offering checked functions. A setter can refuse a bad value. A getter lets others read the value. Then the class always stays valid. Think of a bank counter. You cannot reach the vault, but the clerk checks every deposit. The balance is private. Deposit is the only way to add money. It refuses an amount of zero or less. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Encapsulation in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.script: The getter reads the age. The setter checks the range. Only an age from zero to one hundred twenty is accepted. Seventeen is accepted. Five hundred is refused. The age is still seventeen. The program prints seventeen. Keep data private. Offer public functions that check the input. A setter can refuse a bad value. The class always stays in a valid state. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A setter that does not check
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in encapsulation?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in encapsulation? Bug of the Day. The setter stores any number. The program prints an age of minus five. The data is private, but the setter gives no protection. Add a check, so that the class stays valid. A setter without a check is the same as a public field. The age of minus five breaks the rules of the class. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: A setter that does not check.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Can you write a safe class in encapsulation?
shorts.script: Can you write a safe class in encapsulation? The vault told the thief, you can only deposit your complaints at the window. Write a Thermostat class. The setter must accept only temperatures from ten to thirty degrees. Write your answer in the comments. Keep data private. Offer public functions that check the input. A setter can refuse a bad value. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pun and challenge.
